summary: Listed as a Copeland lookout in Collier County; the sources read describe the community, not the tower. No build, design or site description found.

evidence.supports: Copeland is a community in eastern Collier County, outside any incorporated town
evidence.quote: Copeland is an unincorporated community located in eastern Collier County

evidence.supports: Community sits at State Road 29 and Janes Memorial Scenic Drive
evidence.quote: It lies at the junction of State Road 29 and Janes Memorial Scenic Drive

evidence.supports: Big Cypress lies east of the community, which sits on the preserve's western border
evidence.quote: Copeland lies along the western border of the Big Cypress National Preserve

evidence.supports: Fakahatchee Strand Preserve State Park lies beside the community, to the east
evidence.quote: wedged beside the Fakahatchee Strand Preserve State Park to the east

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The Eastern US Lookouts page gives only the name and Collier County. The Wikipedia article describes the community and says nothing about a lookout. Two web searches found no tower history. A 2026 Naples Daily News article on Copeland's history (naplesnews.com) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. A Florida Forest Service history booklet (Scribd copy of A Photographic History of the Florida Division of Forestry, 2006) mentions a Copeland Work Center in Collier County used as a fire camp base; it is not known to relate to the lookout and is not used in the story. Copeland does not appear in the cached NHLR Florida list or the cached FFLOS and Forest Fire Lookout Association Florida pages. The story is about 77 words, under the 120-word floor. Recommend leaving the record at status unknown until a Florida Forest Service or Collier County source is found.
